routes.description: Establish the motion through a cumulative case in which the universe's beginning requires a transcendent personal cause, objective moral values require a divine foundation, and the historical facts concerning Jesus are best explained by divine resurrection, while answering principal naturalistic objections.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the cosmological, moral, and resurrection inferences jointly warrant a transcendent personal and moral foundation of reality, and if objections from naturalistic explanation, suffering, source reliability, and methodological limits do not defeat those inferences.

motionBridge.description: The supported cosmological, moral, and historical conclusions must jointly warrant that God exists as the transcendent personal cause and moral foundation of reality.

centralBridges.description: The universe must have begun to exist, and its beginning must require a transcendent, immaterial, personal cause rather than emergence from non-being.
Objective moral values and duties must be real and must require a transcendent divine foundation that evolutionary or social accounts do not supply.
The historical facts concerning Jesus must be established and divine resurrection must explain them better than the proposed natural alternatives.

subsidiaryBridges.description: The existence of suffering must remain compatible with God through the possibility of morally sufficient reasons for permitting it.
Philosophical reasoning must legitimately draw metaphysical consequences from scientifically informed premises without depending on an appeal to unexplained gaps.

routes.description: Defeat the motion by showing that no observed feature of reality requires God, that naturalistic accounts or open scientific inquiry remain available for cosmic origins, morality, and reported miracles, and that suffering conflicts with the proposed loving deity.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the affirmative inferences fail to establish their divine conclusions because their premises or explanatory bridges remain unsupported, natural alternatives remain viable, and the evidential challenge from suffering is not adequately reconciled with an all-loving God.

motionBridge.description: The motion fails if the universe, morality, and historical reports do not require a transcendent personal and moral foundation and the total evidence supplies no adequate basis for God.

centralBridges.description: Cosmic beginning, physical constants, and apparent order must admit naturalistic possibilities without requiring pre-universe causality, purpose, or a divine creator.
Moral conduct and distinctions must be explicable through biological and social development without requiring a divine source or judge.
The resurrection inference must lack sufficiently reliable historical evidence, with ordinary explanations remaining more credible than suspension of natural law.
Apparently gratuitous innocent suffering must count against the existence of the all-loving God specified by the affirmative position.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Claims about reality must be constrained by observation and testable theorizing rather than by metaphysical extrapolation or untestable divine intentions.
A divine entity must not be introduced when simpler explanations remain available in principle or scientific inquiry has not exhausted natural accounts.

sections.title: Cosmic Origin, Causality, and a Personal First Cause
sections.rationale: This issue contains the principal clash over whether the universe began, whether causality applies to that beginning, whether net-zero or successive-universe accounts alter the origin problem, and whether any required cause is personal and transcendent.

sections.title: Objective Morality and Its Foundation
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether objective moral values and duties exist, whether evolutionary and social accounts explain only moral behavior or also binding validity, and whether a transcendent divine foundation is required by the motion.

sections.title: Resurrection Evidence and Miracle Inference
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether the empty tomb, reported appearances, and origin of Christian belief are historically established, whether the sources are reliable, and whether divine resurrection is warranted over natural explanations.

sections.title: Suffering and Divine Goodness
sections.rationale: This issue matters because apparently gratuitous innocent suffering is offered as evidence against an all-loving God, while the opposing route requires showing that God could have morally sufficient reasons for permitting it.

sections.title: Scientific Explanation, Philosophy, and Divine Necessity
sections.rationale: This issue governs whether scientific evidence may support premises with theological consequences, whether metaphysical reasoning legitimately extends beyond empirical inquiry, and whether natural explanation makes God unnecessary without merely appealing to future discovery.
